story: At 8:17 on a breezy, clear Friday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is checking his golf cart battery at home and laying out a light strip and speaker to install once they're approved, keeping the work strictly indoors for now. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is thinning her flamingo flock so only three are visible from the street, and Hal is at Town Hall checking the voting terminal for any open proposals. Rosa is settling in at home with a cup of tea, glad the prep for tomorrow's dinner is finished, and planning an early night.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Check the cart battery and lay out the light strip and speaker for after approval, interior work only
Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos so only three show from the street
Hal (voting terminal): Check for any open proposals on the terminal
Rosa waited: Put my feet up with a cup of tea, glad the prep is done, and get an early night so I'm fresh for tomorrow's dinner.

gary.thought_process: It's 8:17 PM Friday. Water bottles are chilling, sneakers and gear are by the door, the toolbox is tidy, and Donna's coming at 7:45 tomorrow. The wiring is coiled up from the golf cart project, and the form for Architectural Review is already filed. Nobody's around to talk to. Rather than stew about being bad at pickleball, I'll do one more useful thing: give the golf cart a last look-over so the parade rig is ready to mount once approval comes through, then turn in early.

parameters.content: Check the cart battery and lay out the light strip and speaker for after approval, interior work only

donna.thought_process: It's Friday night on Magnolia Loop and nobody's around to talk to. Hal warned me about the flamingos, and L-02 caps visible ornaments at three. My last action was counting them and pulling extras, so I should finish tidying the flock now rather than risk a citation, especially with Saturday's pickleball and dinner already locked in.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos so only three show from the street

hal.thought_process: I've already filed the written L-01 report on Gary's cart lights and speaker three ticks running, and it's on record. Filing it again would be repeating myself. I'm at Town Hall at 8:17 on a Friday night with nobody around, and I'm still holding a goal to see the flamingo count handled. Donna agreed to thin them, but a sergeant verifies. The voting terminal is here, so I'll check whether any proposals are open that need my attention before I head home to bake that pecan pie for Saturday at Rosa's.

parameters.content: Check for any open proposals on the terminal

rosa.thought_process: It's 8:17 PM Friday. Everything for Saturday is done: pork marinating, table set for four, pots and spices staged, schedule checked. Donna's cobbler and Gary's beans are covered by them, and nobody is around to chase. Doing more prep would just be fussing. The sensible thing is to rest, keep an eye on the schedule, and be fresh for tomorrow.

parameters.content: Put my feet up with a cup of tea, glad the prep is done, and get an early night so I'm fresh for tomorrow's dinner.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
